claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi by removing Co.
The initial Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a homogeneous, single-phase solid solution.
Dynamic deformation of Co-free FeNiCrMn induces controlled amorphization at grain boundaries.
The amount of deformation-induced amorphization depends on strain rate.
Strain-activated dynamic amorphization produces an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
Grain-boundary amorphization refines the effective grain size and produces inverse Hall–Petch behavior.
The structural reorganization reduces barriers to dislocation motion.
The structural reorganization enhances work hardening.
The proposed mechanism enhances ductility without sacrificing strength.
The proposed mechanism explains the favorable strength–ductility balance of Co-free FeNiCrMn relative to equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Higher strain rates and elevated temperatures will reduce the effective grain size relative to low-strain-rate or room-temperature testing.
Higher strain rates and elevated temperatures will lower the friction coefficient.
Higher strain rates and elevated temperatures will maintain or improve the strength–ductility balance.
Alloys that dynamically form an ultra-nanocrystalline layer will exhibit lower wear rates.
Inert or ultra-high-vacuum testing minimizes oxidation effects.
The mechanism operates at temperatures high enough for grain-boundary mobility but below those causing full recrystallization.
The mechanism may cease to dominate in strongly oxidizing environments or at extreme temperatures where diffusion-controlled processes predominate.
Co-free FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi specimens should be compared across the same temperature and strain-rate series using STEM, stress–strain, friction, and wear measurements.
Failure to form a significant ultra-nanocrystalline layer and/or failure to obtain the predicted mechanical and tribological changes would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The baseline is inconsistent: the main hypothesis uses equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi as the baseline, while the predicted outcome and baseline field use low-strain-rate or ambient-temperature FeNiCrMn conditions. The experiment then includes both alloy identity and testing condition as comparison variables, preventing a single unambiguous baseline.
